subject: English
q: Patients with high blood pressure are advised to abstain ______ salt-rich food.
explanation: ‘Abstain’ takes ‘from’: one abstains from something.

subject: English
q: All government departments must comply ______ the new procurement rules.
explanation: ‘Comply’ is followed by ‘with’ when it means to obey a rule or order.

subject: English
q: The clerk was accused ______ forging official records.
explanation: One is accused of an offence; ‘charged’ takes ‘with’, but ‘accused’ takes ‘of’.

subject: English
q: The spectators began to jeer ______ the referee after the disputed decision.
explanation: ‘Jeer’ (to mock loudly) is followed by ‘at’.

subject: English
q: Candidates must refrain ______ using mobile phones in the examination hall.
explanation: ‘Refrain’ takes ‘from’ before the thing one avoids doing.

subject: English
q: The party claims to have always adhered ______ its manifesto.
explanation: ‘Adhere’ in the sense of sticking faithfully to a rule or belief takes ‘to’.

subject: English
q: The residents objected ______ the construction of a plaza in the park.
explanation: The verb ‘object’ is followed by ‘to’, not ‘against’.

subject: English
q: Water consists ______ hydrogen and oxygen.
explanation: ‘Consist of’ names the parts that make something up (‘consist in’ means ‘to have as its essence’).

subject: English
q: The opposition insisted ______ a full debate on the budget.
explanation: ‘Insist’ is followed by ‘on’ (or ‘upon’), never ‘for’.

subject: English
q: The municipal committee must find a safer way to dispose ______ the city’s waste.
explanation: ‘Dispose of’ means to get rid of; ‘off’ is a common spelling-based error.

subject: English
q: The flood deprived thousands of families ______ their homes.
explanation: One deprives a person of something.

subject: English
q: Heavy fog prevented the aircraft ______ landing.
explanation: ‘Prevent’ takes ‘from’ before a gerund: prevent someone from doing something.

subject: English
q: Young people should not indulge ______ extravagance.
explanation: ‘Indulge’ is followed by ‘in’ when it means to allow oneself a pleasure.

subject: English
q: Having no one else to trust, she confided ______ her elder sister.
explanation: To tell one’s secrets to a trusted person is to ‘confide in’ that person.

subject: English
q: The finance secretary was asked to account ______ the missing funds.
explanation: ‘Account for’ means to explain or give a reckoning of something.

subject: English
q: The new policy aims ______ reducing the fiscal deficit.
explanation: Before a gerund, ‘aim’ takes ‘at’ (aim at doing); ‘aim to’ is followed by an infinitive.

subject: English
q: After a long discussion, the committee arrived ______ a unanimous decision.
explanation: One arrives at a decision or conclusion; ‘arrive to’ is always wrong.

subject: English
q: The minister refused to comment ______ the leaked report.
explanation: ‘Comment’ is followed by ‘on’ (or ‘upon’) the matter discussed.

subject: English
q: We congratulated him ______ his promotion.
explanation: One congratulates a person on an achievement.

subject: English
q: In view of the emergency, the chairman dispensed ______ the usual formalities.
explanation: ‘Dispense with’ means to do without or set aside something.

subject: English
q: It is pointless to dwell ______ past mistakes.
explanation: To think or speak at length about something is to ‘dwell on’ (or ‘upon’) it.

subject: English
q: The Chief Justice presided ______ the full-court meeting.
explanation: One presides over a meeting, court or ceremony.

subject: English
q: After much effort we prevailed ______ him to withdraw his resignation.
explanation: ‘Prevail on/upon someone’ means to persuade; ‘prevail over’ means to defeat.

subject: English
q: Pakistan subscribes ______ the principle of peaceful coexistence.
explanation: To agree with or support an idea is to ‘subscribe to’ it.

subject: English
q: The injured labourer later succumbed ______ his wounds.
explanation: ‘Succumb’ (to give way or die) is followed by ‘to’.

subject: English
q: The government refused to yield ______ the demands of the protesters.
explanation: To give way to pressure or a demand is to ‘yield to’ it.

subject: English
q: When negotiations failed, the workers resorted ______ a strike.
explanation: ‘Resort’ in the sense of turning to a means of action takes ‘to’.

subject: English
q: The shopkeeper deals ______ second-hand books.
explanation: To trade in a commodity is to ‘deal in’ it (‘deal with’ means to handle).

subject: English
q: He was reluctant to part ______ his father’s old watch.
explanation: One parts with a possession but parts from a person.

subject: English
q: My views on this matter differ ______ yours.
explanation: Things that are unlike ‘differ from’ each other; ‘differ with’ means to disagree with a person.

subject: English
q: I cannot agree ______ you on this point.
explanation: One agrees with a person, but agrees to a proposal.

subject: English
q: After a week of talks, the union agreed ______ the management’s proposal.
explanation: To accept a proposal or suggestion is to ‘agree to’ it.

subject: English
q: The figures in the ledger do not correspond ______ those in the bank statement.
explanation: In the sense of ‘match’, ‘correspond’ takes ‘to’ (or ‘with’); ‘correspond with’ a person means to exchange letters.

subject: English
q: His grandfather died ______ cholera during the epidemic.
explanation: One dies of an illness.

subject: English
q: She has been suffering ______ migraine for years.
explanation: One suffers from an illness or condition.

subject: English
q: It took him months to recover ______ the shock.
explanation: ‘Recover’ is followed by ‘from’ an illness, loss or shock.

subject: English
q: The new treatment cured him ______ his chronic cough.
explanation: A person is cured of a disease or habit.

subject: English
q: The new assistant relieved the manager ______ much of his routine work.
explanation: To take a burden away from someone is to ‘relieve them of’ it.

subject: English
q: The doctor warned him ______ overeating.
explanation: One warns a person against (or of) a danger; ‘warn from’ is incorrect.

subject: English
q: No employer may discriminate ______ an applicant on the basis of religion.
explanation: To treat someone unfairly is to ‘discriminate against’ them (‘discriminate between’ means to distinguish).

subject: English
q: Every citizen must abide ______ the law of the land.
explanation: To obey or accept a rule or decision is to ‘abide by’ it.

subject: English
q: Careless driving often results ______ fatal accidents.
explanation: ‘Result in’ introduces the consequence.

subject: English
q: Much of the damage to the bridge resulted ______ poor maintenance.
explanation: ‘Result from’ introduces the cause.

subject: English
q: The secretary promised to attend ______ the complaint at once.
explanation: To deal with or look after a matter is to ‘attend to’ it; ‘attend’ without a preposition means to be present at.

subject: English
q: The law prohibits shopkeepers ______ selling cigarettes to minors.
explanation: One prohibits a person from doing something.

subject: English
q: Heavy fines have not deterred motorists ______ speeding.
explanation: ‘Deter’ takes ‘from’: to discourage someone from doing something.

subject: English
q: Her friends tried to dissuade her ______ resigning.
explanation: One dissuades a person from a course of action.

subject: English
q: Diplomats are exempted ______ paying customs duty.
explanation: ‘Exempt’ is followed by ‘from’ an obligation.

subject: English
q: Many English words are derived ______ Latin.
explanation: Something is derived from its source.

subject: English
q: A few careless errors detracted ______ an otherwise excellent report.
explanation: To reduce the value of something is to ‘detract from’ it.

subject: English
q: The speaker kept digressing ______ the main topic.
explanation: One digresses from a subject.

subject: English
q: The court ordered the factory to desist ______ polluting the river.
explanation: ‘Desist’ (to stop) is followed by ‘from’.

subject: English
q: He graduated ______ the University of the Punjab in 2015.
explanation: One graduates from an institution (and in a subject).

subject: English
q: The peasants rebelled ______ the oppressive landlords.
explanation: One rebels against authority.

subject: English
q: She has applied ______ a post in the Foreign Office.
explanation: One applies for a job, and applies to the organisation offering it.

subject: English
q: The relief agency supplied the villagers ______ tents and blankets.
explanation: One supplies a person with things (or supplies things to a person).

subject: English
q: The board entrusted her ______ the task of drafting the report.
explanation: One entrusts a person with a task (or a task to a person).

subject: English
q: The suspect was charged ______ murder.
explanation: A person is charged with an offence.

subject: English
q: For want of evidence, the court acquitted him ______ all charges.
explanation: One is acquitted of a charge.

subject: English
q: He was convicted ______ fraud and sentenced to five years.
explanation: A person is convicted of an offence.

subject: English
q: I have known him for years and can vouch ______ his honesty.
explanation: To guarantee someone’s character is to ‘vouch for’ it.

subject: English
q: He spent the rest of his life trying to atone ______ his mistakes.
explanation: One atones for a wrong.

subject: English
q: We sympathise ______ the victims of the earthquake.
explanation: ‘Sympathise’ takes ‘with’.

subject: English
q: The university conferred an honorary degree ______ the scientist.
explanation: An honour or degree is conferred on (or upon) someone.

subject: English
q: The Governor conferred ______ his advisers before announcing the decision.
explanation: In the sense of ‘consult’, ‘confer’ takes ‘with’.

subject: English
q: It is unfair to impose your views ______ others.
explanation: Something is imposed on (or upon) someone.

subject: English
q: Illegal settlers had encroached ______ state land along the canal.
explanation: To intrude gradually on property or rights is to ‘encroach on’ (or ‘upon’) them.

subject: English
q: The country embarked ______ an ambitious programme of reform.
explanation: One embarks on (or upon) a project or journey.

subject: English
q: Society frowns ______ those who break their promises.
explanation: To disapprove of something is to ‘frown on’ (or ‘upon’) it; ‘frown at’ describes a facial expression directed at someone.

subject: English
q: Hawks prey ______ small birds and rodents.
explanation: An animal preys on (or upon) another.

subject: English
q: The opposition was quick to capitalise ______ the government’s blunder.
explanation: To take advantage of something is to ‘capitalise on’ it.

subject: English
q: The old woman dotes ______ her grandchildren.
explanation: To be excessively fond of someone is to ‘dote on’ (or ‘upon’) them.

subject: English
q: The failure of the scheme was attributed ______ poor planning.
explanation: A result is attributed to a cause.

subject: English
q: Many young graduates aspire ______ careers in the civil service.
explanation: To have an ambition is to ‘aspire to’ (or ‘after’) something.

subject: English
q: The government finally acceded ______ the teachers’ request.
explanation: To agree to a request is to ‘accede to’ it.

subject: English
q: Buildings in earthquake zones must conform ______ strict codes.
explanation: To obey a rule or standard is to ‘conform to’ (or ‘with’) it.

subject: English
q: After the strike ended, the factory reverted ______ normal shifts.
explanation: To return to a former state is to ‘revert to’ it; ‘revert back’ is redundant.

subject: English
q: The minister alluded ______ corruption without naming anyone.
explanation: To mention indirectly is to ‘allude to’ something.

subject: English
q: A modest man never boasts ______ his achievements.
explanation: ‘Boast’ is followed by ‘of’ (or ‘about’).

subject: English
q: He has always hankered ______ fame.
explanation: To have a strong desire for something is to ‘hanker after’ (or ‘for’) it.
